issues.issue: Ceasing all monthly deductions on Overloan Protection has to be reconciled with Section 9's rule that deductions are due on every Monthly Calculation Date until the Age 100 Anniversary (c067).

"No additional loans or loan repayments will be allowed" contradicts the Loan Repayment provision permitting repayment at any time while the policy is in force (c099), and sits oddly with c101's requirement that excess loan balance be repaid on exercise.

The provision imposes a one-time Overloan Transaction Charge and then trails off mid-sentence with "There is no additional charge for this benefit or for any of the automatic", leaving the charge scheme incomplete on its face.

"After we receive your written request to surrender the policy, no insurance will be in force" works with Section 6's denial of Death Proceeds after a surrender request (c046) but neither says what happens if the request is later withdrawn or rejected.

Condition (c) refers to "the Minimum Face Amount shown in Section 1," but Section 1 states only a Minimum Total Face Amount and a Minimum Basic Face Amount (c010), so the referenced figure does not exist.

The right-of-first-refusal bar on transfers for consideration has no time limit, no price mechanism and turns on "information satisfactory to us," so what defeats a transfer of ownership is left at large.
This restriction on transfers for consideration is hard to square with Section 18, which lets the owner assign any interest by written notice without anyone's consent (c123).

The text is broken mid-provision ("Gonsent-of-any-~beneficiary... s.not.reauired..f.there.is..no0 'Insured, your estate will be the Beneficiary'"), so the default-beneficiary rule and the consent rule cannot be read as sentences.
Payment "in equal shares" to surviving beneficiaries has to be reconciled with the application's "% Share" designation (c176), which contemplates unequal shares.

The freedom to "assign any interest in this policy without the consent of any person other than an irrevocable Beneficiary" is qualified only by "except as otherwise provided," and Section 17 (c119) blocks collateral or absolute assignments for consideration.
The adjustment is to be made "by the most recent Cost of Insurance charge deducted under Section 9," a phrase that does not state a workable formula for recomputing the face amount.

The opening of the incontestability clause is missing ("the Issue Date, except' for-any™p insurability"), so the length of the basic contestable period and its exception cannot be read from the provision.
A payment "limited to the higher of" two amounts reads as a floor rather than the cap the sentence purports to impose, so the measure of recovery on a contested face amount is uncertain.

The integration clause is immediately undercut by "such additional requests may become part of the policy," which conflicts with Section 22's requirement that any change be in writing signed and countersigned by officers (c134).
The signed-writing requirement for any change is contradicted by Section 4's reserved right to make unilateral "reasonable adjustments to the terms or conditions" of the policy (c040).
"Clerical errors" is undefined and the correction right is unilateral, so the line between correcting a slip and altering a term is left to the insurer.
The opening obligation is unreadable ("nniversary-we:will:send-you=-without-charge ach-Policy Year which-ineludes"), so the timing and trigger of the annual statement cannot be stated from the text.

A fee of up to $50 for a report requested "at any other time" sits against the next paragraph's promise of "one report annually without charge" (c138), leaving overlapping and inconsistent charging rules.
Defining "We" as Phoenix "or its subsidiaries" for rider purposes departs from Section 3, where "we" refers only to the Company (c038), leaving the obligor under the rider unclear.
Limitation 3 forbids a Requested Benefit "less than the lower of 25% of the policy face amount or $50,000," a double comparative that is awkward to apply against limitation 4's separate cap.

"Expected to result in the insured's death within six months based on evidence satisfactory to us" combines a prognosis judgment with the insurer's own satisfaction, and gives no objective standard for either.
